_comment: Hand-checked story bank. Each beat is one narrated line plus the graphic shown while it plays. Show types: title, year, number, text, versus, end.

stories.title: He Sold 10% of Apple for $800
stories.description: In 1976 Ronald Wayne co-founded Apple with Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak, then sold his 10% stake back twelve days later.

beats.say: This man owned ten percent of Apple, and sold it for eight hundred dollars.
In 1976, Ronald Wayne founded Apple with Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak.
He even drew the company's first logo.
But just twelve days later, he got nervous about the debt, and sold his stake back for eight hundred dollars.
Apple is now one of the most valuable companies on Earth.
On paper, that ten percent would be worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
Wayne has said he doesn't regret it. Would you? Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: Blockbuster Laughed at Netflix
stories.description: In 2000 Netflix offered to sell itself to Blockbuster for $50 million. Blockbuster said no.

beats.say: Blockbuster could have bought Netflix for fifty million dollars.
In the year 2000, Netflix was a small DVD by mail company losing money.
Its founders flew to Dallas and offered to sell it to Blockbuster for fifty million dollars.
Blockbuster passed. It had thousands of stores and didn't see the threat.
Ten years later, in 2010, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy.
Netflix is now worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
One meeting changed everything. Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: Kodak Invented the Digital Camera
stories.description: A Kodak engineer built the first digital camera in 1975. Kodak filed for bankruptcy in 2012.

beats.say: Kodak invented the digital camera, and it destroyed Kodak.
In 1975, a Kodak engineer named Steven Sasson built the first digital camera.
It weighed about eight pounds and took twenty three seconds to save one black and white photo.
But Kodak made its money selling film, so digital looked like a threat, not an opportunity.
Others moved fast. Kodak moved slowly.
In 2012, the company that invented digital photography filed for bankruptcy.
Inventing the future isn't enough. You have to sell it. Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: Yahoo Passed on Google Twice
stories.description: Yahoo reportedly passed on buying Google in 1998 and again in 2002, then sold its core business to Verizon for about $4.5 billion in 2017.

beats.say: Yahoo had two chances to buy Google, and said no both times.
In 1998, Google's founders reportedly offered their search engine to Yahoo for about one million dollars.
Yahoo passed.
In 2002, Yahoo came back and talked about three billion. Google wanted five. Yahoo walked away again.
In 2017, Yahoo sold its core business to Verizon for about four and a half billion dollars.
Google's parent company is now worth over two trillion.
Sometimes the cheapest deal is the one you skip. Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: The Billion Dollar Pizza
stories.description: On May 22, 2010, Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 bitcoin for two pizzas.

beats.say: These two pizzas cost more than a billion dollars.
On May twenty second, 2010, a programmer named Laszlo Hanyecz wanted to prove bitcoin could buy something real.
He paid ten thousand bitcoin for two pizzas.
Back then, that was worth about forty one dollars.
When bitcoin passed one hundred thousand dollars, those coins were worth over one billion.
May twenty second is now celebrated as Bitcoin Pizza Day.
Most expensive meal ever? Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: The Label That Rejected The Beatles
stories.description: On January 1, 1962 the Beatles auditioned for Decca Records. Decca turned them down.

beats.say: A record label once turned down The Beatles.
On New Year's Day 1962, the band auditioned for Decca Records in London.
They played fifteen songs in about an hour.
Decca said no, and signed another band instead.
Legend says an executive told their manager that guitar groups were on their way out.

show.text: "Guitar groups are on the way out"

beats.say: The Beatles went on to sell hundreds of millions of records.
Biggest miss in music history? Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: How Nokia Lost the Phone War
stories.description: Nokia was the world's biggest phone maker. In 2013 it sold its phone business to Microsoft, which wrote off most of it two years later.

beats.say: Nokia once sold more phones than anyone on the planet.
For more than a decade it was the world's biggest phone maker.
Then in 2007, the iPhone arrived. Nokia bet that people would keep loving keyboards.
By 2013, Nokia sold its phone business to Microsoft for about seven billion dollars.
Two years later, Microsoft wrote off almost all of it.
From king of phones to a footnote in under ten years.
Who is the next Nokia? Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: Coca-Cola Changed Its Recipe
stories.description: In April 1985 Coca-Cola replaced its formula with New Coke. After 79 days of backlash, the original came back.

beats.say: Coca-Cola once changed its secret recipe, and America lost its mind.
In April 1985, Pepsi was winning taste tests, so Coke launched a new sweeter formula.
In blind tests, people actually liked it more.
But real customers were furious. The company got hundreds of thousands of angry calls and letters.
After just seventy nine days, Coca-Cola brought the original back.
Sales of the classic recipe went up. Some people still think it was a marketing trick.
Blunder or genius? Tell me below, and follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: $1.75 Billion Gone in 6 Months
stories.description: Quibi raised $1.75 billion for short-form streaming and shut down about six months after launch in 2020.

beats.say: This app burned through almost two billion dollars in six months.
Quibi raised one point seven five billion dollars from Hollywood's biggest names.
The idea: expensive TV shows, cut into ten minute episodes, only for your phone.
It launched in April 2020, right when everyone was stuck at home, watching on big screens.
You couldn't even share clips. And free short videos were everywhere.
About six months after launch, Quibi shut down.
Money can't buy timing. Follow for more billion dollar blunders.

stories.title: Xerox Gave Away the Future
stories.description: Xerox PARC built a computer with windows, icons and a mouse in the 1970s. Apple and Microsoft turned those ideas into empires.

beats.say: Xerox built the modern computer, and let others get rich from it.
In 1973, Xerox's research lab built the Alto, a computer with windows, icons, and a mouse.
Xerox was a copier company, and it didn't know what to do with it.
In 1979, a young Steve Jobs got a tour of the lab.
Apple's Lisa and Macintosh followed. Then Microsoft Windows.
Today, almost every computer on Earth works that way.
Great ideas are worthless in the wrong hands. Follow for more billion dollar blunders.
